title.narrative: Investing for impact to end Tuberculosis and HIV

description.narrative: Ghana - TB/HIV - Ministry of Health of the Republic of Ghana - Ghana Mal-MOH. This program has the following goals: To reduce TB incidence by 25% from 148 in 2018 to 111 per 100,000 population by 2025. To reduce by 35% the 2018 TB mortality rate baseline of 52 deaths per 100,000 population by 2025. To reduce the proportion of TB-affected families who suffer catastrophic cost due to TB from 64% in 2016 to 0% in 2025. To achieve HIV epidemic control and the fast track treatment targets of 90-90-90 by 2023. To reduce new HIV infections by 42% by 2023. The objectives of this program are: Universal access to better and efficiently managed quality healthcare services. Universal access to better and efficiently managed quality healthcare services. To early screen, detect and enrol into treatment 90% of estimated all forms of TB, i.e increase treatment coverage from 33% in 2019 to 90% by 2025. To early detect and enrol into treatment 90% of estimated RR/MDR TB cases among new and previously treated cases by 2025. Reduce avoidable maternal, adolescent and child deaths and disabilities. Reduce avoidable maternal, adolescent and child deaths and disabilities. Increase access to responsive clinical and public health emergency services. To attain higher treatment success for all forms of TB from 85% in 2018 to at least 90% by 2025 through improved quality clinical care and community TB care and to attain high treatment success rate of RR TB and/or MDR-TB from 64% in 2017 to 90% by 2025. Increase access to responsive clinical and public health emergency services. To provide latent TB treatment or TB preventive Treatment (TPT) to TB contacts and for PLHIV without active TB. To increase the estimated PLHIV who know their status from 58% in 2019 to 90% by 2023.. To increase the % of people newly diagnosed with HIV initiated on ART from 81% in 2019 to 95% in 2023. To increase the % of HIV-positive women who received ART during pregnancy and/or labour and delivery from 75% in 2019 to 95% in 2023. To increase the % of HIV-exposed infants receiving a virological test for HIV within 2 months of birth from 65% in 2019 to 90% in 2023. To increase the % of PLHIV on ART who initiated TB preventive therapy among those eligible during the reporting period to 49% in 2023. To increase ART initiation among HIV-positive KP (MSM) and (FSW) to 95% in 2023. To increase the % of clients on ART who are virally suppressed from 68% in 2019 to 90% by 2023.
